column1: The 25 bp cut to 1.50–1.75% and the move to maintain “ample” reserves via T‑bill purchases and repo operations are consistent with the literature that finds short-run real effects of monetary policy. VAR evidence (Sims, 1992) and liquidity-effect studies (Christiano and Eichenbaum, 1992) indicate that unexpected easing can support output and employment when private investment and exports soften. With inflation running below target and market-based inflation compensation low, an inflation-targeting perspective (Svensson) supports moderate easing to keep inflation and expectations near 2% without undermining credibility. The Desk’s focus on bills and repos is mainly an implementation choice to stabilize money markets under an ample-reserves framework rather than a shift toward balance-sheet-driven stimulus. Dissenting votes and noted global uncertainties point to a cautious but supportive stance overall. sentiment score = 0.25
